text_content:

name: The founders are the first interviewers, and their read is a scorecard rather than a review
text_content:
Routed to: Session 16 (86ajgmjz6)

Her rule is that a founder interviews every finalist and models the no on the candidate who is just fine, the hard-to-name concern. Session 5 kept the founder in the process and refused that no. Pre-opening the founder stage is the last scored stage for every seat, run in the check-in's form of length and place, reading two things only: the non-negotiables, and whether the building can supply what this person needs. Its scorecard is submitted independently and read by the domain lead who decides, like every other. A founder's no names a read or is not a no, and a founder who wants a candidate the lead declined has a structure question for the partners' review rather than a hiring one. The team recommends the stage ends for edge seats at the mechanism reset after dinner's first quarter and continues for lead seats permanently. Two things route to Session 16 specifically: what a founder's own read actually is, since the record gives the founders no training and no anchors and names the founders as the only interviewers pre-opening; and what a partner brings to a table as the customer the house is built around, since the dinner in the room reads exactly that in a candidate and the partners run it.

name: A departure opens a seat, and the pool is read before anyone looks outside
text_content:
Routed to: Session 15 (86ajgmjpw)

Managing out produces a departure, and a departure at Sŏn is a tension re-establishment and not a backfill: thread removal is tension loss, not slot vacancy. Session 5 fixed what happens next. The domain lead may open the seat the day the departure is known, provided the ready-now pool has been read first and the sheet records the reading, and the sheet's field 15 states what the departing node held, because the adjacent nodes are already compensating. If the pool holds someone on the track, that person's practical assessment is the next stage rather than an external search, and for a critical-path seat they take the seat's paid practical in a real service before they hold it, scored like any candidate's, because the floor will not honor a paper readiness. The succession commitment binds from the first tension loss after dinner opens, and an outside hire for any lead seat after dinner's first quarter carries a written line on the partners' page stating that no one in the pool is on the track and how far the nearest person is. Session 15's managing-out design should end where that line begins, and should not let an exit produce a seat opened externally with the pool unread.

name: Hiring assessments never become a person's record, and one hire arrives with a written line the check-in reads
text_content:
Routed to: Session 14 (86ajgmjk1)

Session 5 closed the packet at the hire and kept it in the applicant system: no scorecard, no assessment content, and no verdict travels to the person page, so a performance conversation months later reads what the person and their lead wrote at check-ins and never what an interviewer thought before the person started. Session 14's performance work must not reach back for the hiring record. One exception travels deliberately and is not an assessment: the candidate's own answer to the fourth read, what they said they need from the building, written on the page at the offer as the baseline the first check-in reads against. And one case arrives already flagged: where a domain lead hired against a founder's fourth-read concern, the lead writes on the packet what the building will supply that the founder said it could not, that line goes to the partners' review record, and the person's first check-in reads it. Session 14 says what happens when the building did not supply it, which is a building failure and not the person's.

name: The compensation architecture sits on the hiring timeline's critical path, and the salaried line decides who gets a last round
text_content:
Routed to: Session 13 (86ajgmjey)

The record's transparency sheet is handed at the first interview with everything needed to decide, including the compensation mechanics, and the record elsewhere says the mechanics are still being finalized. The leads are in the building at least six weeks before dinner's gate, so their first interviews fall months before Session 13 can ratify the architecture: the record's own sheet cannot be handed as specified until it lands. That makes the architecture a hiring gate and not a parallel track, and the record does not say so. Session 5 states the record's compensation commitments on the sheet and no architecture, carries no figure and no percentage anywhere, and recommends that the mechanics field may read "being finalized" for the pre-opening leads' first interviews and never for an offer; the founders rule on that interim. Session 13 also decides which seats are salaried, because the record's last round, the dinner in the room, applies to leadership and salaried seats, so the salaried line decides who gets one. And cross-strand fluency's recognition is already an open item in the record; Session 5 adds cross-period fluency beside it (see the Session 8 and Session 13 carryover on that marker).

name: Recruiting hands Session 12 two feedback events it does not yet know how to deliver
text_content:
Routed to: Session 12 (86ajgmjba)

Two of recruiting's triggers are performance feedback to a person in the house, and Session 5 fixed where they go and not how they are given. First, a scorecard returned without a named read goes to the Maitre d as a re-training trigger, and the interviewer does not run another stage until the re-training is done; that is the tell of an untrained interviewer, and it is also a lead or a team member being told their work was not good enough. Second, a decline at the packet that contradicts every stage's scorecard goes to the leads' review as a calibration read, which puts one person's judgment in front of the other lead. Session 12 designs how both are delivered inside the check-in's form and the leads' review's, without turning either into a verdict, and says what the lead does when the pattern repeats. The constraint from Session 4 holds: the lead may not write on the person page outside a check-in, and neither of these events is a check-in.

name: Every recruiting surface is bound by canon rules whose register canon does not name, and by the languages the house speaks
text_content:
Routed to: Session 11 (86ajgmj7c)

Canon is the source of truth for every word, its language constant applies in any internal communication, and its forbidden lexicon applies in all contexts with no exceptions, yet its register matrix names six surfaces and none of them is a recruiting or employee-facing surface; "you" is specified for customer-facing contexts, and a candidate reading a posting is not a customer in that moment; and canon does not say whether a document handed to a candidate is a brand context, which decides whether the Korean terms stand unglossed in front of a stranger. The team read one register and could only mark it held for canon's owner. Alongside it sits a set of language obligations Session 11 owns: the seat sheet lives on the team home in every language the team speaks, the transparency sheet is handed in the candidate's interview language, every stage is run by someone who speaks the language the candidate chose, the answer set exists in every language the process runs in, and every posting states which languages the process itself is available in. Session 11 designs the communication system those obligations run on and closes what it can of the register question with canon's owner.

text_content:

name: An open seat is a load reading on a domain, and a departure is a tension re-establishment
text_content:
Routed to: Session 9 (86ajgmj07)

Session 5 routed recruiting's failures into the diagnostic cadence rather than into a recruiting scoreboard. A seat open past its response window with no candidate advanced goes to the leads' review as a load reading on the domain, not as a recruiting failure. A seat open past three consecutive leads' reviews goes to the partners' review as a possible node-overload entry, because the adjacent nodes have been compensating for three weeks. A seat the lead wants to hold open rather than fill below the bar goes to the leads' review as a slack reading, since the bar holds only if the house can absorb the hole at tempo. A seat opened by tension loss goes to that week's leads' review as one line: what the node held and what the adjacent nodes are carrying, because a departure is a tension re-establishment problem and not a backfill problem. And a decline at the packet that contradicts every stage's scorecard goes to the leads' review as a calibration read, not as an appeal. Session 9's diagnostic method should read these as signals of the same kind as the five failure modes scorecard, and should say what a diagnosis does with a domain that produces them repeatedly.

Provenance: Session 5, session task 86ajgmhm4, page sections 4.4, 6.3, 8.6, and 12.3 (P14, P28, P46, I22), Operating System doc 2ky45bmy-17253.

name: Cross-period fluency is the second development marker the record needs and does not name
text_content:
Routed to: Session 8 (86ajgmhxx), Session 13 (86ajgmjey)

The record names cross-strand fluency as the real development marker, makes it visible in the web as more connections, and recognizes it in compensation as meaningful, with its recognition a named open item. Everything else in the record requires a second marker: one restaurant and one brand met at different times of day, late night as dinner's own later register, one system and four moods, same foundation and four registers, each period continuing the one before it. All of it asks the same person to hold a different register at a different hour. Recruiting hit this because one labor pool staffs the service periods, the seat sheet's service-period field is where a person's second period is recorded, and the first period expansion is the first succession event, so the dinner cohort is being hired into a fluency the record has not named. Session 5 recommends naming cross-period fluency as a development marker parallel to cross-strand fluency, recorded on the person page as connections. Session 8 places it structurally; Session 13 decides whether it is recognized in compensation, alongside cross-strand fluency's own open recognition.

name: No runner or host seat can be opened until the inward-facing floor strand has a lead
text_content:
Routed to: Session 8 (86ajgmhxx)

name: The work style grid is out of recruiting and may return only as a self-awareness tool
text_content:
Routed to: Session 7 (86ajgmhrz), Session 10 (86ajgmj2u)

Her grid crosses introvert and extrovert with task and people orientation to produce Analyzer, Director, Collaborator, and Promoter. Session 5 kept it out of recruiting entirely: not as a scorecard attribute, not as an interview question, not as a team-composition target. The reasoning was structural rather than cultural. Service pressure selects hard for assertion and expression, the people interviewing are the people the room rewarded, and a hiring system that lets the room's read stand as the hiring read reproduces the room; the answer is inward-facing seats opened and filled on their own competency requirements with equal rigor and never as a step toward outward-facing seats, measurement held by the stack and accounted for by the Operations Lead, and the paid practical scored by rubric by an assessor who does not decide. The grid may return inside the house as a self-awareness tool, and where it returns is Session 7's and Session 10's to place. If either session brings it back, it comes back as language people use about themselves and never as an instrument that reads a person for a seat.

Provenance: Session 5, session task 86ajgmhm4, page sections 3.4 and 14 (P8, P9, I26), Operating System doc 2ky45bmy-17253.

name: The person page exists before the first shift, and the start date has conditions
text_content:
Routed to: Session 7 (86ajgmhrz)

Recruiting creates the person page at the offer accepted, not at the first shift, and writes ten entries to it and nothing else: the seat and its sheet version, the strand, the domain lead by seat, the decision-rights range as accepted, the service periods, the start date, the mentor connected before arrival, the ninety-day plan's start, the first unlock the sheet names, and what the candidate said they need from the building, in their own words, captured at the first interview as the fourth read. That last entry is the baseline the first check-in's "what is in the way" question reads against, and Session 7 designs the ninety-day plan so its six check-ins carry it. No assessment scorecard ever travels to the page; the packet closes at the hire and its record stays in the applicant system. The start date carries conditions a lead may not commit against: the mentor is connected, the uniform and locker are ready, the training platform carries the seat's first modules, the ninety-day plan's first check-in falls on a pre-service window the lead works, the mechanics field is filled, and the person's first shift is not a new period's first service and is not coverage before the record's own bar that no one touches a table until they are ready. A start date that cannot be set inside a month of acceptance because the mentor or the modules are not ready is a training-infrastructure load, not a recruiting one.

name: What Session 6 inherits as settled, and the five instruments it must not build
text_content:
Routed to: Session 6 (86ajgmhnt)

Session 5 closed the decision structure that Session 6's hiring loop runs inside, and Session 6 should extend it rather than reopen it. There is no hiring committee and no hiring meeting: the decision is the domain lead's, on a complete packet of independently submitted scorecards, made the day the packet completes, with the answer sent the same day, and Greenhouse refuses a decision on an incomplete packet. There is no recruiting seat: the coordination is the stack's, the candidate-experience standard is the Maitre d's, the record is the Operations Lead's. No assessor decides and no decider assesses alone; a decline names a read or a must-have from the sheet and nothing else; a lead who is one of two first-interview interviewers requires the second. A hole is held rather than filled below the bar, and the leads' review carries it as a slack question. Five instruments are refused with the mechanism that does their work named in each case: her work style grid (which may return only as a self-awareness tool in onboarding or team development, never in the interview), the résumé review and the take-home, the hiring committee and the hiring meeting, her recruiter's interview loop and scorecard, and the bias-neutralizing copy tool.

Provenance: Session 5, session task 86ajgmhm4, page sections 8.6, 9.1, and 14 (P8, P40, P46, P48, P68, I26 to I30), Operating System doc 2ky45bmy-17253.

name: The first interviewers are untrained by the record's own definition
text_content:
Routed to: Session 6 (86ajgmhnt)

The record requires trained interviewers, because asking a good question and reading the answer is a learned skill and not an instinct that arrives with a title. The training infrastructure is the learning platform on which any qualified team member creates modules, and the platform does not exist before the team does. Session 6 writes the training's content and, with the founders, writes how the first interviewers are trained before the platform exists. name: Who supplies what: Claude never generates Brandon's interiority or Sŏn's intent
text_content:
Status: routed, standing, governs every session including this one.

This program is an assistant, not an automation. The distinction is not a courtesy. It is a rule about what may be written down.

Claude never generates

Facts about Brandon, Dominic, or the chef partner. Values, work style, strengths, motivations, failure modes.

Facts about what Sŏn intends. Mission, vision, operating principles, what good looks like on the floor, what will and will not be tolerated.

Any decision.

Claude has memory and context sufficient to produce very plausible versions of all of the above. Plausible and unendorsed is the worst available outcome, because it reads as true, is assembled from true fragments, and gets acted on. A document about how Brandon appears is not a document about Brandon.

Claude generates

Analysis. Structure. Translation. Argument. Record.

The three-way sort: what transfers, what adapts, what does not apply, and why. Rebuilding her instruments for a different substrate: hourly, shift-based, four dayparts, embedded compensation, no headcount growth. Holding the standard when a definition goes soft. Writing it up and filing it correctly.

The rule that carries this

Claude may propose. Claude may not record a proposal as a decision.

A proposal goes in the Open section, named as awaiting Brandon. It does not go in the body as settled. S1 did this correctly with the founder 1:1 cadence: proposed weekly and quarterly, marked open, awaiting confirmation. That is the pattern.

When a session needs a decision Brandon has not made, it stops and asks. It does not propose and proceed.

The gradient

Ownership is not constant across the program.

Heavily Brandon. S1 (done). S2, founding documents. S16, founder time and energy. These are interiority and intent. Claude structures the question and refuses to answer it.

Heavily structural. S13, rebuilding compensation architecture around a 21.5% embedded share. S6, interview loop mechanics. Claude does most of the building, against decisions Brandon makes.

Joint, and this is where the value is. Brandon proposes, Claude pushes, Brandon decides. It does not work if either side is asleep.

The specific S2 trap

Brand canon is an input to the founding documents. It is not a substitute for the decision.

Sŏn's mission is a choice. It is not a synthesis of existing brand language, however elegant that synthesis would be. A Claude in S2 that assembles a mission statement out of "life share not market share," "the building is not the asset, the customer is," and the playground philosophy has committed exactly the failure this item exists to prevent.

Note on the session briefs

Several session tasks say "Sŏn output (draft): [artifact]." That phrasing hands the pen to Claude by default and it is a drafting error in the build-out, not an instruction. This item governs where it conflicts with a brief. S1 already resolved one such conflict correctly by weighting the carryover over the task. That was right.

name: Levels and ladders: does a single house need them at all
text_content:
Routed to: S8 Team structures (86ajgmhxx), S13 Formal review + compensation (86ajgmjey)

Her checklist assumes job ladders and levels, clearly communicated. Her whole review and compensation apparatus hangs off them.

Sŏn has none, and the open question is not when to build them. It is whether a single 120-seat house should have them at all.

The case against: levels in a company that does not grow are a promise the company cannot keep. They manufacture the expectation of a ladder and then supply four rungs.

The case for: without levels there is no legible answer to "what is my path," and a strong candidate will ask on day one.

Downstream of 86ajgnh8n (Sŏn does not scale to 7,000). If lateral daypart movement is the real structure, then levels may be the wrong shape entirely and something else has to carry what a ladder carries elsewhere.

Do not default to building them because the book assumes them.

Surfaced S1.

name: The 1:1 has no shift-native form: her cadence assumes desks
text_content:
Routed to: S4, Ch2 Operating cadence (86ajgmhjr). Secondary: S12 (86ajgmjba)

Her entire cadence rests on the 1:1: weekly or biweekly, rarely rescheduled, shared agenda, notes, actions, quarterly goals tracked inside it. It is the load-bearing member of her operating system.

It is written for salaried knowledge workers with desks, calendars, and control over their own hours. It does not survive contact with shift-based hourly staff who are on the clock only when the room is open and who are paid for the shift, not the meeting.

The function is not optional. The form is. S4 has to produce a shift-native equivalent or Sŏn will simply not do 1:1s, which is what almost every restaurant does.

Open questions S4 must answer:

When does it happen and is the person paid for it
What replaces the shared 1:1 document for someone who does not open documents
Is quarterly even the right unit, or are daypart and season the native cycles
Does the pre-shift lineup, which already exists daily, absorb part of this function

Note the inversion: Sŏn's problem is not too few team meetings. Lineup and family meal already happen daily. The problem is that the daily meeting carries no structure.

name: Work style demand differs by daypart: one labor pool, four profiles
text_content:
Routed to: S5 Recruiting (86ajgmhm4), S6 Hiring (86ajgmhnt), S8 Team structures (86ajgmhxx)

Her work style grid (introvert/extrovert against task/people oriented, producing Analyzer, Director, Collaborator, Promoter) is a self-awareness tool. Used as a team-composition tool in a restaurant it produces a specific, predictable distortion: service pressure selects hard for Director and Promoter. A floor staffed by pattern-matching to the room ends up with almost no Analyzers, at which point nothing gets measured and no one notices.

The four dayparts make this sharper. They do not demand the same profile.

Good Energy, morning. Repetition, precision, prep, low interaction density, high consequence for small errors. Analyzer and Collaborator work.
Dosi, lunch. Throughput under a clock. Director work.
Dinner. The full range. The only daypart that genuinely wants all four.
Luxx, late night. Energy, presence, the room. Promoter work.

A single house running four dayparts is not staffing one work-style profile. It is staffing four, from one labor pool, with substantial overlap between them.

Interacts with 86ajgmmc3 (four dayparts is not four teams).

name: Sŏn does not scale to 7,000: her headcount premise does not apply
text_content:
Routed to: all sessions. Read before every sort.

She wrote for a company going from 200 people to 7,000. "Scaling to the call," her frame for evaluating whether a person can grow into a larger role, only means something in a company that inflates around them.

Sŏn opens at roughly full size and stays there. A line cook in year three is a line cook in a 120-seat house. There is no org chart bloating underneath anyone. The role does not grow because the company does not.

This is not a limitation. It is a different compounding mechanism and it is Sŏn's actual thesis. Sŏn compounds in customer relationships and system knowledge, not headcount.

Consequences that must be tested in every remaining session:

Career development cannot be sold as promotion. There is no ladder above a station in a single house.
Retention is the whole game. A departure removes accumulated customer knowledge that took years to build and cannot be rehired. Her hiring chapter is calibrated for volume. Sŏn's must be calibrated for permanence.
Her review machinery sorts people for advancement. Sŏn's must deepen people in place. Different instruments wearing the same name.
The four dayparts are the only real lateral surface. Movement at Sŏn is across dayparts, not up levels.

Anything in the book that presupposes headcount growth is suspect by default.

Logged as decision D1.8, S1.
